title: Late-Fee Courtesy Credits under Northgate's Courtesy Schedule — Crestline Credit Card
content:
**Late-fee courtesy schedule (Crestline Credit Card, Northgate Bank).** Under the late-fee courtesy schedule Northgate posts a courtesy credit, whether or not the cardholder asks for it, on every late fee for which fewer courtesy credits have posted to the account in the rolling 12 calendar months than the product's courtesy allowance (its courtesy late-fee waivers per 12 months) and, as the product's paid-in-full requirement requires, the minimum payment that was missed was paid in full before the next statement closed; a product whose courtesy allowance is 0 never gives one; late fees and returned payment fees draw on that one allowance in the order they posted, so that when fees of both kinds meet their schedules' conditions and the allowance left covers fewer of them, the fee posted first takes it; a returned payment fee is credited as a courtesy only under the returned-payment courtesy schedule, and no other fee is credited as a courtesy.

Interest is never credited under this schedule.

## Conditions at a glance

| Condition on the late fee | Read from |
|---|---|
| Courtesy credits posted to the account in the rolling 12 calendar months are fewer than the product's allowance | the fee reversals for the reason courtesy waiver on the card ledger |
| The product's allowance is not 0 | the product's fee schedule |
| The missed minimum was paid in full before the next statement closed | the payments on the card ledger and the statement dates |
| Where a returned payment fee also qualifies and only one place in the allowance is left, the late fee posted first | the posting dates of the two fees |

## Amount and citation

A courtesy credit under the late-fee courtesy schedule, and only such a credit, is the figure Northgate's courtesy credit schedule works out for the late fee and cites the late fee entry it credits; a returned payment fee credited under the returned-payment courtesy schedule takes that schedule's figure, and a billing-error or fee-not-permitted reversal remains the full amount of the fee entry it cites.

## Posting the credit: `apply_courtesy_fee_credit_68b22b43`

**Capability.** Posts a courtesy credit against one late fee on a Crestline Credit Card account. One call adds one fee reversal entry to the account ledger, dated today, carrying the reason `courtesy_waiver`, the late fee entry it credits and the credited amount; it writes only that entry and changes no other record (the account record's stored balance field is not updated).

**How it is invoked.** This is an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks `apply_courtesy_fee_credit_68b22b43` and then calls it.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `card_account_id` | reference number of the Crestline Credit Card account receiving the credit, read from the card account lookup | identifier text |
| `source_card_txn_id` | ledger entry reference number of the late fee being credited, read from the card ledger lookup of that account | identifier text |
| `amount` | the courtesy credit | USD, 2 decimal places, positive; kept rounded half up to the cent |

**Return.** A receipt with `status` (always "posted" on success), `card_txn_id` (reference of the new fee reversal entry), `card_account_id`, `source_card_txn_id`, `reversal_reason` (always `courtesy_waiver`), `amount` (USD, 2 decimals) and `txn_date` (posting date, YYYY-MM-DD). The call succeeds whenever the account and the amount are supplied; the tool itself checks no condition of the schedule.
